messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate from Control Plane (org-lookup + auth) observed across hosted API. Rolling error rate: 12% over 5m, latency p95 spike to 2.4s. Pager sent to oncall.
alice: Oncall here, seeing spike on the dashboards. Which services are firing? link: <https://observability.redwood.com/d/ctrlplane/errors>
bob: org-lookup service showing timeouts to the config DB and increased retry flood. Error logs: `grpc: deadline exceeded` across callers.
carol: paging from incidents: customers experiencing 503s when creating routes and during token validation. Support queue heat-up — Anna, any customer reports?
anna: Yep, multiple customers filed errors via in-app — most are 503s on POST /v1/routes and 401/500 combos on auth introspect. Adding examples to the support thread.
support-bot: Added incident tag and bumped severity to P1 per SOP.
alice: Quick mitigation plan: 1) Enable cached org-lookup fallback for 30m 2) Route auth traffic to secondary region pool 3) Throttle background sync jobs 4) Scale org-lookup horizontally. Anyone object?
david: Agree. Quick note: last deploy to config service ~1h ago (PR #8467) touched DB connection pooling. I want to check connection saturation first before scaling.
bob: Running a quick query on connection stats.
bob: ```
# pg_stat_activity snapshot
SELECT count(*) AS active, state FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY state;
-- result: active=250 idle=20  (max_connections=260)
```
bob: Looks like pool exhaustion on config DB. Retries from org-lookup are cascading  -> timeouts -> 5xx upstream.
carol: Can we temporarily increase DB pool size and reduce retries? Alice, can you authorize config change?
alice: I authorize a short-term increase on the pool to 400 and set client retry backoff to linear 1000ms -> 2500ms. Make sure to rollback after we stabilize.
david: Applying change now. Patch: `config-service: db.pool.max=400` -> deploying to staging then prod canary.
david: ```
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/config-service DB_POOL_MAX=400 --record
kubectl rollout status deployment/config-service
```
david: Canary passed in us-west-2. Rolling to remaining replicas.
anna: Support: notifying impacted customers with temporary degraded mode note. Using template: "We’re experiencing intermittent 5xx errors; mitigation in progress; no data loss expected." Sending now.
alice: Also enabling cached-artifact fallback in gateway for org lookups. This will return last-known mapping for 5m TTL.
bob: ```
# gateway config tweak
curl -X POST https://gateway-admin/config -d '{"org_lookup_behavior":"cache_on_error","cache_ttl":300}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN"
```
bob: Config accepted, rolling.
carol: Observability: after DB pool bump and gateway fallback, error rate dropped to 4.3% in the last 2m, p95 down to 680ms. Still noisy but improving. Keep throttles in place.
alice: Good. Next: investigate why connection pool exhausted. David, can you share number of backend workers and qps breakdown?
david: ```
# current metrics snapshot
org-lookup: qps=4800, avg_latency=120ms
config-service: qps=2000, conn_in_use=248, max_conn=260
```
david: It looks like background maintenance jobs spike every minute causing bursts. I'm going to disable noncritical cron syncs for 15m.
david: Cron jobs disabled. Let's watch.
carol: Observability shows a further drop — error rate 2.1% and decreasing. Some customers still affected; support escalations reduced.
anna: Customers updated twice. A few enterprise customers asked for RCA and ETA; ETA for full recovery? 
alice: ETA ~20-30m to return to baseline. We'll keep config rollback plan ready if instability recurs.
bob: Fingers crossed. I also opened a short-term ticket to add circuit-breaker on org-lookup callers to prevent cascade.
alice: Good call. Post-mortem owners: David (root cause: DB pool + cron bursts), Bob (mitigations + circuit-breaker), Carol (customer comms), Anna (support follow-ups). I will run the incident doc.
support-bot: Noted. Taking ownership of customer follow-ups.
carol: Reminder: schedule handoff to next oncall in 25m. @alice, can you do the formal handoff or assign to @bob if you need rest?
alice: I'll do the handoff after 25m. Current state at handoff: error rate ~1.2%, p95 180ms, canary rollback not needed. Actions remaining: monitor for 60m, validate cron re-enable plan, and prepare RCA draft.
bob: I'll stay on standby for 2h in case the pool re-saturates.
alice: Thanks team. Closing the pager for now but keeping channel open for updates. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident P1 resolved: Control Plane org-lookup timeouts — mitigation applied. Summary: DB pool increased, cron disabled, gateway fallback enabled, customer notices sent. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-15 09:00 UTC. Link: <https://status.redwood.com/incidents/1774123456>
